problem_statement: The Malaika-Ali Responsive Blog Website Template is a static editorial blog with a homepage hero, a Most Recent Posts card grid, a Suggested Posts feed, a pet feature article at blog.html, a travel category route at category.html, sidebar categories and newsletter, and a shared masthead navigation rendered on every page from a site-wide link registry. Add a new cross-page Field Guides section: (1) a guides.html collection page built from the same rounded card grid the homepage already uses (six guide cards, each with local JPG imagery, an h2.card_title heading, a short description, and a link into an existing story); (2) a Field Guides entry registered once in the shared navigation registry (nav-links.js) so its a.nav-link appears consistently on the homepage, the blog page, and the new page; (3) a compact guide-index strip summarising the collection, shown on the home page and the collection page, that must stay within the document width on a 390px phone; and (4) a lightweight reader-path picker on the home page whose readout updates to preview which Field Guide the chosen theme opens next when a theme chip is clicked. The new work must reuse the existing Blogger visual language and shared header/footer chrome rather than introducing a bespoke off-system layout.
required_content: Add a new Field Guides collection page at guides.html that reuses the existing shared .cards/.card/.grid homepage card pattern (rounded white cards, local JPG imagery, an h2.card_title heading, a short description paragraph, and a link into an existing story).

The Field Guides page must present at least six guide cards titled Reconnecting With Nature, Quality Time With Family, Living Well With Pets, Travelling On A Budget, The Art Of Happiness, and Minding Your Mental Health, threading the existing nature, family, pet, travel, happiness, and mental-health stories.

Register a Field Guides entry in the shared navigation registry (nav-links.js) so the shared site-nav renderer stamps an a.nav-link Field Guides item on the masthead of every page, including the homepage.
The Field Guides nav-link and page must wrap in the existing shared masthead navigation and footer chrome and must not be a bespoke standalone layout, cheat-sheet, or link dump.

Preserve the existing Blogger brand, Home/Category/Latest navigation, Most Recent Posts cards, Suggested Posts feed, pet article, travel category list, sidebar, newsletter forms, footer, and mobile menu.

Use the existing font variables, gradient button treatment, white/light-gray editorial sections, rounded cards, and local JPG imagery. Do not add remote assets, generated images, new frameworks, or build steps.
The Field Guides page must remain readable on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile within the original template's existing small mobile overflow tolerance.

Add a compact guide-index strip (four labelled metric cells summarising the collection) on the home page and the Field Guides page, laid out so it stays within the document width on a 390px mobile viewport (no horizontal overflow beyond tolerance) and matches the existing white rounded-card visual language.

Add a reader-path picker on the home page with theme chips (Nature, Family, Travel, Mental health) and a live .path-status readout; clicking the Travel chip must update the readout to preview the 'Travelling On A Budget' guide (the readout must reflect the actually-clicked theme, not a stale default).
design_constraints: Treat this as a small cross-page section addition for an existing editorial blog, not a full rebrand.
Build the new page from the shared homepage card grid so it inherits the site's rounded-card rhythm.
Use the existing Blogger color system: white/light-gray sections, dark gray body text, midnight accent, and the existing sky gradient for hover or CTA emphasis.
Register the new section once in the shared nav registry so the nav-link stays consistent across pages, rather than hand-coding a divergent menu on the new page.
Avoid bespoke off-system headers, cheat-sheet layouts, external media, decorative blobs, and card styles that clash with the current rounded blog cards.
state_constraints: Desktop, tablet, and mobile home states must render the existing hero, navigation, recent cards, suggested posts, and local imagery, show the registered Field Guides nav-link, and show the guide-index strip and reader-path picker.
The guide-index strip must stay within the document width on the 390px mobile home and mobile collection states (no horizontal overflow beyond tolerance).
Clicking the Travel chip on the reader-path picker must update the .path-status readout to preview the 'Travelling On A Budget' guide.
The Field Guides page at guides.html must render the shared masthead, the six-card guide grid, and the shared footer on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile.
The Field Guides nav-link must appear on the homepage, the blog page, and the Field Guides page (cross-page nav consistency).
No captured state may emit disallowed console errors or failed network requests.

change_completion: The new Field Guides page presents at least six guide cards with the required titles.
A Field Guides nav-link is registered in the shared nav registry and renders cross-page (home, blog, guides).
The reader-path picker readout updates to preview the chosen theme's guide after a chip is clicked.
design_consistency: The Field Guides page and guide-index strip reuse the shared rounded card grid, fonts, gradient accent, and section rhythm.
The added page wraps in the shared masthead and footer chrome rather than a bespoke off-system layout.
responsive: The guide grid and guide-index strip stack cleanly on tablet and 390px mobile within the known overflow tolerance.
Text remains readable without overlapping cards, nav, images, or footer content.
regression: Existing hero, navigation, recent cards, suggested posts, article/category routes, newsletter forms, and local JPG assets remain intact.
No captured state emits disallowed console errors or failed network requests.

author_notes: L1 Consistency (design_continuity) cross-page add: a new Field Guides collection page built from the shared homepage card grid plus a Field Guides entry registered in the shared nav registry so the nav-link renders cross-page. Product-grade acceptance uses enforce_console_errors (max 0) and cross-page dom_assertions (a.nav-link Field Guides on Home and the new page, plus the six-card grid structure) beyond text-signal matching. Mobile overflow tolerance stays at 24px for the template's pre-existing trait.
